purpose: Register of the five new geological hypotheses designed in the 2026-10-02 continuation session, each naming its layers, physical signature, uncatalogued-fault rationale, difference from prior work, ordinal expected benefit, implementation cost, status and stop rule. No numeric DTI benefit is claimed for any entry; the only measured quantities live in new-hypothesis-validation.json (blocked SGMC-proxy protocol + live-score consistency).
validation_gate: A hypothesis may not influence a release candidate until it (a) beats a seed-matched random emission on a majority of the 5 blocked SGMC-proxy folds and (b) is reported with the live-score consistency check. Beating the SGMC proxy is necessary, not sufficient: no available proxy ranks the 24 live artefacts above chance (offline-proxy-audit.json), so no entry here authorises a submission slot.

hypotheses.title: Cross-family azimuth (orientation) coherence
hypotheses.layers: structure tensors (sigma=300 m) of official det_elev, rtp, iso_grav_anom, cond_surf, depth_to_base_surf; lidar product strike + coh100 channels
hypotheses.transform: A_ij = coh_i * coh_j * cos^2(theta_i - theta_j), averaged over family pairs; cos^2 (not cos^2 of doubled angle) so perpendicular lineaments score 0
hypotheses.physical_signature: Faults are linear: independent fields should be locally anisotropic AND strike the same way at a fault corridor; magnitude overlap alone cannot distinguish coincidence from structure
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: Catalogue faults were mapped largely from magnitude evidence (airphoto/lidar scarp + geophysical gradients); orientation agreement across independent families is a genuinely independent discriminator, and catalogue mapping is weakest where no single magnitude signal is strong
hypotheses.difference_from_prior: No layer, transform or sibling artefact compares azimuths across families; build_edge_consensus.py is magnitude-only; lid_strike is exposed raw in the 95-layer bank but never cross-checked
hypotheses.stop_rule: does not beat random on a majority of the 5 blocked SGMC folds

validation_result.verdict: REJECTED. As a standalone emission the orientation-agreement score scores ~10x below a random emission on every blocked fold, and its live-score consistency is null (lidar-gated variant anti-correlated). The stop rule fires: no further standalone investment, no slot.

hypotheses.title: Shallow-residual potential-field edges
hypotheses.layers: official rtp band; upward continuation at 500 m and 2000 m; edge magnitude; depth_to_base_surf cover-thickness context
hypotheses.transform: residual = rtp - upward_continuation(rtp, h); residual edge magnitude (Sobel, sigma=2 px); thick-cover variant multiplies by normalised depth_to_base_surf
hypotheses.physical_signature: exp(-2 pi h / lambda) separation: upward continuation removes short wavelengths (shallow sources); the residual keeps the uppermost ~1 km of crust, so its edges in thick cover are young cover-cutting structures
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: The catalogue is dominated by mapped bedrock structure; deep-persistent magnetic edges are mostly already catalogued. A Quaternary fault cutting alluvial cover is a shallow short-wavelength source that the residual isolates and the catalogue systematically lacks
hypotheses.difference_from_prior: The layer bank has native-support gradients and one 150 m upward-continued magnitude layer (ext_TMI_up150); no residual, residual-edge or cover-context product exists. H-35 proposes the complement (deep persistence across heights)
hypotheses.stop_rule: same as H-38; habitat-feature follow-up must survive unforced 15-fold leave-one-family-out nested CV above 0.437391

validation_result.habitat_nested_cv_unforced_folds_selecte: 0/15 (ranks 38/96 for 500 m norm |rho|=0.3791 and 40/96 for thick-cover norm |rho|=0.3643 vs top-8 cutoff 0.5548)
validation_result.verdict: REJECTED as a standalone emission (0/5 folds vs random on the blocked SGMC proxy) AND rejected in the 15-fold leave-one-family-out habitat nested-CV follow-up: in unforced selection both H-39 variants rank 37-50/96 by univariate |Spearman| (well below the k=8 cutoff 0.5548 and k=14 cutoff 0.5070), are selected in 0/15 folds, and leave nested-CV Spearman unchanged at 0.437391 (delta = 0.000000); when force-appended to the ridge fit inside every fold, the raw layer degrades CV at every |G| (0.383478, delta = -0.053913 at |G|=6,000) while the [0,1]-normalized layer changes CV by only +0.008696 (0.446087, k=8, beta=+0.2726) at |G|=6,000 and degrades at |G|=15,000 (0.384348, delta = -0.024348). Closed: neither promoted into the habitat model nor emitted into a submission raster.

hypotheses.title: Fine-scale seismicity lineament density
hypotheses.layers: USGS ComCat ANSS earthquakes M>=2.5 1960-present (external, free, official), kernel-smoothed at 5 km and 10 km; NOT the competition ieq/deq bands
hypotheses.transform: event-density kernels at 5/10 km radius, depth-weighted variant, lineament orientation of dense alignments
hypotheses.physical_signature: microseismicity lines up on active blind faults; swarms and linear event chains mark structures that lack surface expression
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: the official stack's earthquake channels smooth at a 100 km radius (n100), which erases fault-scale structure; uncatalogued ACTIVE faults should carry fine-scale lineations the official bands cannot express
hypotheses.difference_from_prior: no seismicity layer at fine spatial support exists anywhere in the group's work; the official ieq/deq bands prove the signal class matters but at 10-20x coarser support
hypotheses.caution: Coolbaugh et al. (2002, A Geothermal GIS for Nevada, GRC Transactions) measured earthquakes as the LOWEST-weighted evidence layer in their weights-of-evidence permeability model, so fine-scale seismicity may be a weak standalone signal; the official 100 km-smoothed bands' presence in the feature stack is not evidence that finer support helps

obtainability.evidence: FDSN count endpoint answered 15802 events (M>=2.5) and 692 (M>=4.0) for the wider AOI box 1960-01-01..2026-10-01; text format streams correctly

hypotheses.status: proposed; acquisition automated this session; catalogue not yet fetched (sandbox has no egress to earthquake.usgs.gov)
hypotheses.stop_rule: smoothed density fails to beat random on the blocked SGMC proxy or adds no live-score consistency

hypotheses.title: Direction-resolved fault-tip and step-over lobes
hypotheses.layers: trace skeletons of labels.tif + SGMC traces (both in-repo); tip azimuths; anisotropic wing-crack lobes (30-45 deg off tip) and relay ramps between overlapping like-dipping traces
hypotheses.transform: tip/stepover geometry -> anisotropic distance-decay lobes (vs the isotropic clusterprior)
hypotheses.physical_signature: splays and relay strands nucleate at tips and stepovers of known faults; stepovers host ~40% of the INGENIOUS area's favourable structural settings and terminations ~17% (Faulds & Hinz 2015 and the 2026 INGENIOUS-area update)
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: the staff ruling says new faults include newly mapped geometry of existing systems; the missing short traces physically must sit at tips and stepovers, which the catalogue truncates
hypotheses.difference_from_prior: sibling H19-1 used isotropic sigma=1.8/2.5 km tip/stepover Gaussians; this repo's clusterprior is isotropic proximity to long faults. The delta is direction-resolved lobes from trace azimuths - unimplemented anywhere
hypotheses.stop_rule: direction-resolved lobes do not beat the isotropic clusterprior out-of-fold on the blocked SGMC proxy

hypotheses.title: Playa / basin-margin discharge association
hypotheses.layers: det_elev flatness + local relief adjacency; cond_surf; in-repo GDR spring/well CSV; distance-to-basin-floor and basin-margin-edge density
hypotheses.transform: basin-floor flatness mask -> margin distance/edge density; combined with spring density and conductivity edges
hypotheses.physical_signature: Great Basin Quaternary faults bound basins and control discharge; the weights-of-evidence geothermal GIS work (Coolbaugh et al. 2002, GRC Transactions; Coolbaugh et al. 2005, NBMG Map 151) found favourability in shallow-groundwater / basin-floor settings, and high-temperature systems prefer NE-trending structures within 5 km
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: catalogue mapping concentrated in bedrock/uplands; basin-margin strands under alluvium near playas are systematically under-mapped - the same sparse-historical-fieldwork premise the catalogue-gap hypothesis rests on
hypotheses.difference_from_prior: the spring layers are pure distance/density; no playa, basin-floor or margin-geometry term exists in the 95-layer bank or any sibling artefact
hypotheses.expected_benefit: low-medium (ordinal only; targets geothermal systems more than fault traces)
hypotheses.stop_rule: basin-margin proximity does not enrich the SGMC-proxy faults out-of-fold
